newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Southern says RDP funds outperform targets.
newsitem.headline: Southern says RDP funds outperform targets.

text.p: South African life insurer Southern Life said on Wednesday that funds set up to invest in projects associated with the country's Reconstruction and Development Programme (RDP) had outperformed their targets.

The RDP portfolio of four funds, collectively called Futuregrowth, saw assets under management rise 42.5 percent to 1.2 billion rand as a flood of cash from retirement fund investors poured into them.
The Futuregrowth Equity Fund, which invests in black empowerment firms, beat its target of eight percent ahead of the inflation rate by posting returns of 58.9 percent.
The Futuregrowth Income Fund, which focuses on investment in water, electrification and housing finance, has returned 14.5 percent since it was founded three years ago.

Futuregrowth Balanced Fund achieved a three-year return of 17.2 percent and the newest of the funds, Futuregrowth Property Fund, beat internal forecasts to post a non-annualised 11.3 percent return over the second half of 1996.
Futuregrowth co-ordinator Michael Leeman said the portfolio had invested more than 230 million rand directly into RDP projects in the last six months of 1996.

These included 66 million rand in support of black empowerment grouping the NEC's buy of a stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd, 36 million rand in a rights issue by black investment vehicle Real Africa group and nine million rand in the Trans Caledon Tunnel Authority.
Leeman said the Futuregrowth portfolio was set to have two billion rand of assets under management by the end of 1997.
"Futuregrowth has also recently been opened to investors for the first time, after previously being targetted only at pensions and provident funds," he said.

The RDP programme is also expected to increase in momentum in 1997 with state telecommunications firm Telkom acquiring a strategic equity partner and airline Sunair and resorts group Aventura being wholly privatised.
